opex.name: Marketing, selling & administrative
opex.note: Sales teams, advertising and the back office — up 10% on launch spending.

opex.name: Acquired IPR&D
opex.note: Research bought in from other companies, charged at once — $0.14 of the quarter's EPS.

opex.name: Asset impairment & restructuring
opex.note: Related to anticipated litigation payments — there was no such charge a year ago.

footerNote: Reported (GAAP) figures throughout; Lilly's non-GAAP net income was $3,541M (EPS $3.92). The release reports figures to one decimal place; they are rounded to whole millions here.
oneTimers: Acquired in-process R&D of $154M ($0.14 of EPS), up from $97M a year ago. Lilly counts IPR&D in both its reported and its non-GAAP figures.

Asset impairment, restructuring and other special charges of $435M ($0.38 of EPS), related to anticipated litigation payments, with no such charge a year ago. Lilly's non-GAAP net income of $3,541M (EPS $3.92) excludes this charge, along with net losses on equity securities and amortization of intangible assets.
The year-ago quarter's revenue included $579M from the sale of rights for Baqsimi — excluding it, Q2 2024 revenue grew 46% rather than the reported 36%.
otherDetail: Net other expense of $198M — $146.3M of net interest expense and $51.3M of net other expense, the latter driven by net losses on investments in equity securities.

segments.name: Mounjaro
segments.note: The diabetes shot (tirzepatide) — revenue more than tripled on strong demand, higher realized prices and the launch of the KwikPen outside the U.S.

segments.name: Zepbound
segments.note: The weight-loss shot (tirzepatide), launched in the U.S. in November 2023 — already $1.2B a quarter.

segments.name: All other medicines
segments.note: Everything else — Verzenio ($1.3B, +44%), Trulicity ($1.2B, -31%), Jardiance, Taltz and Humalog. Down 5% overall, partly because the year-ago quarter included $579M from selling the rights to Baqsimi.

takeaways.text: Mounjaro ($3.1B, +215%) and Zepbound ($1.2B, launched November 2023) together brought in $4.3B of the $11.3B total — two versions of the same drug, tirzepatide.
takeaways.title: Two shots are 38% of revenue

takeaways.text: Lilly lifted full-year 2024 revenue guidance from $42.4–$43.6B to $45.4–$46.6B, and reported EPS guidance by $2.05 to $15.10–$15.60, on the strength of Mounjaro and Zepbound.
takeaways.title: Guidance raised by $3B

takeaways.text: Lilly booked a $435M asset impairment, restructuring and other special charge related to anticipated litigation payments, plus a $154M acquired IPR&D charge — and operating income still rose 75% to $3.7B.
takeaways.title: A litigation charge in the quarter

verdict: Lilly's revenue rose 36% to $11.3B as Mounjaro more than tripled to $3.1B and Zepbound added $1.2B — and profit jumped 68% to $2.97B, prompting Lilly to raise full-year revenue guidance by $3B.
